reading:
The judges love this line for one gesture: the greeting standing on its own Coming up rail. The Next up tube drops a lit wire onto the sill, the NOW lamp breathes at the left end, airglow rises off the lit run, and below that the page is matte slate and steel. On the landing panel feedback gave it 9.1 ("the owner's Signal Box line language at its best"), interaction 8.5 and style 8.2. Soul called it "one luminous zone, then calm". They also love the one-line setup strip, To do's dated timetable margin, Chat's single left track ending in a lit 'your turn' ring, the Ideas 'line from home' tube, and the Status lamps typed on the glass.

What holds it at #2 (7.52, then 7.81) is placement and affordance, cited again and again:
(1) Reading order. The tube sits left of the headline, so the eye lands on NEXT UP before the question. System, interaction, style, usability and skeptic all asked for this in tour round 3 and again on the landing panel.
(2) The To do tick is a hollow ring that reads as a status lamp, not a button, and amber on the ring reads as 'late', not 'press' (interaction, usability and skeptic in r3, usability on the panel). The main tournament's lessons already say ticks should be square.
(3) The starters scroll sideways on the phone (feedback, interaction, usability, system).
(4) The plates under the rail are small and identical, and names break to three lines (style, type, skeptic, system).
(5) Too much light at the top: the halo on 'planning' plus the board's outer halo edge toward glare. Green share is about 69% (feedback, soul, skeptic).
(6) Small counts stacked beside titles ('4 open / 3 late') (system, type, usability).
(7) Lately added and the lower half of Home are still the old page (feedback, interaction, skeptic).
(8) Several lenses want an instrument on Status. They asked for the moving-coil meter from the Instrumented mutant, with a scale that keeps a $0.04 day from sitting on zero.

Its title 'What needs planning?' was praised as the invitation you cannot answer 'no' to, and faulted for its heavy 8-letter lit word.

What would make it win: keep the sill gesture whole, put the question first, make the plates real boards standing on the sill beside the tube, make the tick look like a box, and carry one lamp grammar plus one head rule through every page, with light only on the lit run, the tube, the key word and live lamps. The main camp already has the solved parts this needs. Desk Terminal, Joined has the needle meter, a To do with square wells, WHO/DUE heads and sans 'was due' words. Backlit Plate has rule-led heads with the count on the baseline. Dessau has a footer legend that teaches the shapes once on every page.

briefs.name: Sill Line, Squared
briefs.hypothesis: Sill Line, Ticked already has the tournament's best single gesture: the greeting standing on its lit week. It lost points only on things the main camp has already solved: reading order, a tick that does not look pressable, stacked tiny counts, an empty Status beside the glass, and a lamp grammar explained on one page only. Fix those with the leaders' own components, rebuilt in steel, slate and ink, and keep the sill, the wire, the lit run and the matte lower page untouched. Then the line keeps its 9.1 feedback and 8.5 interaction scores and gains the system, usability and type points that Desk Terminal, Joined and Backlit Plate win on. It also beats the carried design on the owner's two latest asks: light where the phosphor is, a calmer page everywhere else.
briefs.brief: Start from t3-track-graft's files (x14a-b/variants/t3-track-graft/: templates/*.html, src/*.css built to sheet.css; palette x14a-b/palettes/t3-track-graft.json). Keep the palette tokens. Change only: bubble-them #182536 -> #1a2230 (a warmer ink, per style) and a new token plate-cap #86a9cc. TYPE SYSTEM, written once in sill.css and used on every page: - display 3rem (the greeting headline only) - title 2.25rem (h1 page titles) - head 1.5rem (h2 section heads), all three Archivo condensed (wdth 75) 650, heading colour #ebe6da - body 1rem/1.55 DM Sans, small .875rem, label .75rem Archivo 600 caps at .08em in --label - DM Mono ONLY for clock times, day numerals and table figures, tabular-nums - every relative phrase ('in 7 days', 'was due 5 days ago') in DM Sans - row titles never underlined (underline on hover and focus only) - links underlined in sentence case - no stacked count anywhere: a count sits on its title's baseline HOME, one board, read top to bottom (.home .board): Row 1 spans the board. - An eyebrow line: her screen tile at 2rem, 'Vera', the date in DM Mono .875rem ink-2. - Under it the headline h1.ask-question at display size: 'What needs a plan?'. Its label is still for=text. - The glow on 'plan' keeps the kit's E1 two layers with the outer spread cut by a third (0 0 6px brand/.55, 0 0 22px brand/.22, no third layer). Row 2 is a grid of 7fr / 5fr. - Left: the box (textarea, From row, mic, Send), unchanged inside. The board's outer halo is cut by a third. The board edge becomes 1px line-2 steel with a 1px brand/25% top highlight only, so the frame is no longer green. - Right: the ways to start as a steel branch (graft T3-01 below). It starts at an 'Or start with' junction ring level with the box's top edge. A 2px steel line drops down; each starter is a full-width 44px slate key with a ring stop on the line and a right arrow; the line ends in a T buffer. The junction ring lights brand while the box has text (.ask:has(textarea:not(:placeholder-shown)) .branch-junction). Row 3 is the sill (.coming.sill-foot): everything stands ON the rail. - Left: the Next up tube at hero size (about 26rem wide, 14rem tall glass, scanlines, the E7 bloom at 1.0). Its power lamp drops the lit wire to stop one. - The NOW lamp sits at the board's inner left padding, never past the edge (skeptic). It is a white-hot core in a breathing halo. The lit run goes from NOW to stop one ONLY, with airglow rising off that run alone. Stop one onward is steel #56708c. - Right of the tube, standing on the same rail: the later plans as ink plates (.sill-plate), three to four sharing the remaining width equally with flex:1 and min-width 0, bottom-aligned to the rail, each on a 1px leg to its ring stop. - Each plate's content top to bottom: - a kind ring with the kind word in .75rem label caps - the name in Archivo condensed 600 1.125rem, at most two lines, text-wrap:balance, with   inside proper names ('Mount St. Helens') - who it is for in ink-2 small - the time in a sunk mono well (inset 0 1px 2px #000a, background field), 'in 7 days' in sans beside it - Plate fill is bubble-them with a 2px plate-cap top edge and steel sides, not green. - Above the plates, level with the tube's top, the station board: 'Coming up' at head size with '4 coming' on its baseline in ink-2 and the Calendar note in small ink-3 after it. This fills the glass that was dead before. - 'All plans ->' is the T buffer's own label at the rail's right end. - Day numerals hang BELOW each stop: the DM Mono 1.5rem figure with OCT over SAT in .75rem caps. Below the board: Setup strip (.setup-strip): - Ring 1 is amber and current, rings 2 and 3 steel. Each ring has a 44px hit area. - 'Next: choose your own password ->' with its clause ('so everybody signs in as themselves') as a second line in ink-2 at 64rem and up. - 'All 3 steps' at the row's size. - The strip is slate with a 3px amber left edge, not an amber outline. Then two columns, To do 7fr and Lately added 5fr, each under a RULE HEAD (graft 3). Home To do keeps the timetable rail and becomes the square-tick timetable (graft 2): - The margin carries the date alone ('Sun 27 Sep', DM Mono .8125rem ink-2). - The rail has square stops. - Title, then WHO, then a DUE column in sans with amber 'was due 5 days ago'. - A steady lit NOW tick across the row: no breath, a 1.2s afterglow on load. Lately added comes onto the line language: - A steel rail on the left whose stops are the kind rings (the ring is the lamp, coloured by kind). - The name in body 600, then the kind word after the name in its kind colour at .8125rem (skeptic), then 'for Maya, Theo' in a right column in ink-2. - Rows on the tray, no tint. - The right-aligned grey kind-word column is removed. The kids' wishes stay as one line under To do. Phone (max-width 40rem): - Headline, then box, then the starters stacked as the vertical branch (no sideways scroll, no fade). - Then the tube with its foot band trimmed to the scope's height. - Then the rail turned vertical with the plates as 44px rows beside it. The tube's wire meets that rail. - Coming up keeps a 44px row height. TO DO page (tasks.html), whose head is a head row: - 'Things to do' title with '4 open · 3 late' on its baseline (late in amber, a link), and Add something to do as the one green primary at the right. - Then the Show keys and search. - Then the board under column heads in label caps: 'Due' over the margin, 'Tick when done' over the stops, 'Thing to do', 'Who', 'Due' (words), 'Edit'. - The stop/tick (the _ui.html tick macro and .tick-line .tick): - a 1.375rem square, 4px radius, 2px #56708c edge, filled bg so the rail passes behind it - a 44px hit via ::after inset:-.7rem - on hover and focus-visible: surface-3 fill, a phosphor check stroke at 45%, and the 2px focus ring in brand - aria-label 'Mark done: {title}' - Late tasks keep a steel box. Their amber goes in the words. - The undated task gets a solid square, not dashed. - The NOW divider is a full-width 1px brand line with a 'now' label, steady, with the kit's afterglow. - Done rows (Done filter) show a lit sage check in the square. - Edit folds keep 44px controls. STATUS (status.html): one graphite faceplate (thin 2px bezel, square, 12px radius) holding two windows of scanlined glass side by side (graft 1). - Left: the named lamp board as now (WHO ANSWERS / KEYS / CONNECTED rows of named lamps, '3 OF 4'). Working lamps breathe E20 again. - Right: the moving-coil spend meter, with: - a square-root scale over the day's limit, so a $0.04 day sits about 14% up the arc and is never pinned at zero - the hot needle with halo and white tip - a ghost needle for 'Average day $0.04' - an amber zone from 75% to 100%, and a hatched overrun past the limit - '$0.00 TODAY' in VT323 at the top left - Under the faceplate, one line of big condensed tally figures with their lamps: '5 working · 1 waiting · 2 off · 4 not set up · 1 needs a look'. Zero states are hidden; 'needs a look' is in amber. - 'Change the limit' at the meter's foot. - The sections below (Who answers, Keys, Connected to) keep their short rails, each ending ON its last lamp, under rule heads. IDEAS: - Keep the 'line from home' tube but calm it: station names nowrap, a square-root scale, ticks only at 15/30/60 min, at most six labelled stations, the rest as unlabelled dots. - The head row is 'Ideas' with '12 ideas · 10 on the line' on its baseline. 'Add an idea' is the green primary at the right on the title's baseline. - Rows: name, kind word after it, then DRIVE (bold figure, light unit) and WAY in their own right-aligned columns. PLANS: keep the month's dashed quiet weeks but draw them as part of the line (a 1px dashed steel run with the week range in small ink-3 on it). Open the month on the week holding today. One count that agrees with the list. CHAT: keep the one left track, the margin times and the lit 'your turn' ring, which now gets E4's halo. The family's bubbles are neutral surface-2 with a 3px plate-cap bar, not a navy fill. SETTINGS, the form and setup: section heads become rule heads. The Settings lamps stay as stops on a line ending in a buffer. EVERY PAGE (graft 4): base.html's footer gains the lamp legend line. Its sill line now runs past its own lit stop to a steel buffer. GREEN SHARE: brand stays only on the mark, Send and the primary keys, 'plan', the NOW lamp and the lit run to stop one, the tube, the live lamps, focus, and the 'your turn' ring. Plate edges, board edges, rails and setup rings are steel, amber or ink. Target: Home under 55% green by coloured pixels.
briefs.borrows:
Its own judges' fixes, most-cited first:
(a) Question before the tube. Asked by system, interaction, style, usability and skeptic in tour round 3, and by interaction, style and usability on the landing panel. Fix: headline across row 1, the box in row 2, the tube after them as stop one.
(b) A tick that reads as a box: amber on the words, not on the ring; a 'Tick when done' hint; no dashed undated ring. Asked by interaction, usability and skeptic in r3, and usability on the panel.
(c) Starters stacked on the phone, and a steel branch on desktop. Asked by feedback, interaction and usability in r3, and feedback, system and usability on the panel.
(d) Plates wider and taller, names on two lines at most, no break inside proper names. Asked by style and type in r3, and style, type, system and skeptic on the panel.
(e) Less halo at the top, and a shorter lit run (NOW to stop one only), with the lamp kept inside the board's edge. Asked by feedback, soul and system in r3, soul on the panel, and skeptic in the t3-track-refine fixes.
(f) Counts on the title's baseline, not stacked. Asked by system, type and usability on the panel.
(g) Lately added brought onto the line, kind word after the name. Asked by feedback in r3, interaction and skeptic on the panel, and skeptic and style in r3.
(h) Setup: only ring 1 coloured, 44px rings, the clause shown on desktop, 'All 3 steps' at row size. Asked by skeptic, style, interaction, usability and type.
(i) An instrument on Status with a usual-day scale, and lamps breathing again. Asked by soul and style in r3, and by system, style, interaction, usability and skeptic on the Instrumented mutant.
(j) Calm the Ideas scope. Asked by skeptic on the panel.

From the OTHER camp:
1. Desk Terminal, Joined (r13-idea-1): the moving-coil spend needle with ghost average and hatched overrun. Called 'the most period-true lit instrument on any page' (soul) and 'light as data' (skeptic). Files: x14a-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/status.html (the crt('readout spend-meter …') call from line 59, .readout-avg and .ghost-key) and x14a-a/variants/r13-idea-1/sheet.css (.needle, .needle-core, .needle-halo, .needle-tip, .needle-ghost, the swing keyframes, around lines 3095-3099). Shots: x14a-a/out/r13-idea-1/shots/status.png. Rebuilt on Sill's scanlined spend glass beside the named lamp board under one thin bezel, on a square-root scale. It replaces the right-hand tally column and its 160px of dead slate.
2. Desk Terminal, Joined (r13-idea-1): To do's WHO/DUE column heads, amber 'was due' words in their own right column, and the lit NOW tick across the rows. Called 'the calmest, best-typeset desk' (feedback), with 'To do has a lit NOW tick and amber late words' (interaction). Files: x14a-a/variants/r13-idea-1/templates/tasks.html (.colheads, .ch-who, .ch-due, .due.warn, .now-tick) and sheet.css lines 2751-2758 (.now-tick on the rail). Shots: x14a-a/out/r13-idea-1/shots/todo.png and home.png. Rebuilt: the square well sits ON Sill's rail as the stop itself, so the line's 'the stop is the tick' survives. The due words are set in DM Sans, not Desk's tracked mono, which type faulted.
3. Backlit Plate (r13-idea-2): rule-led section heads, with the condensed head, a 1px lead rule, and the count plus link on the same baseline at the right ('4 plans · All plans ->'), plus its DAY/AT/IN column heads. Praised: 'rule-led condensed heads with the count on the same line' (system 8.4); 'Rule heads carry a figure and a link at the right' (type 7.7). Files: x14a-b/variants/r13-idea-2/templates/_ui.html (the rule() macro) and home.html lines 110-112 and 167 (call rule(…), p.colheads), and x14a-b/variants/r13-idea-2/sheet.css lines 2466-2481 (.rule, .rule::before, .rule > h2). Shots: x14a-b/out/r13-idea-2/shots/home.png. Rebuilt in Sill's steel line-2 rule at head size 1.5rem, with no lead-rule stub before the title. Plate's underlined row titles are NOT taken.
4. Dessau Phosphor (r13-wild-3): the footer shape key, which teaches the page's marks once on every page. Files: x14a-a/variants/r13-wild-3/templates/base.html lines 130-132 (span.foot-key with k-circle, k-square, k-bar, k-tri) and x14a-a/variants/r13-wild-3/sheet.css lines 1997-2000 (.foot-key). Shots: x14a-a/out/r13-wild-3/shots/home.png (foot). Rebuilt as this line's lamp legend: '● now · ○ to come · ✓ done · ◐ needs a look · ◌ not set up · ▮ yours'. The now lamp has its real E20 halo, 'yours' is a small ink plate swatch with the plate-cap top, and the line is .75rem label caps in --faint. Sill has no base.html in its variant, so the designer copies the repo's base.html into templates/ to add it. This answers 'the six-signal key lives only on Status' (style, system, interaction, usability, skeptic).

From the ledger: T3-01, the ways to start as a steel branch off the box, from t3-track-refine2 Trued, Relit ('high-style line art', feedback; 'the best use of the line language', skeptic). Files: x14a-a/variants/t3-track-refine2/templates/home.html (the 'Or start with' junction and branch markup) and x14a-a/variants/t3-track-refine2/src/branch.css. Shots: x14a-a/out/t3-track-refine2/shots/home.png and home-phone.png. Hung from the box's right side on desktop and stacked under it on the phone.
briefs.avoids:
It answers its own judges' complaints:
- 'The tube sits left of the question, so the eye lands on NEXT UP first' (interaction, skeptic, system, usability, style).
- 'A first-timer reads an amber ring as a status lamp, not a button' (usability, interaction).
- 'The starters scroll sideways on the phone' (feedback, system, usability).
- 'Plates are small and identical, and names break to three lines' (style, type, skeptic).
- 'The halo on planning outshines the tube; the greeting edges toward glare; 69% green' (soul, feedback, skeptic).
- 'The now lamp's run stabs out of the board's left edge' (skeptic).
- 'Stacked tiny counts beside titles' (system, type, usability).
- 'Lately added reads as the old page; right-aligned kind words sit oddly' (feedback, skeptic, style).
- 'An amber-outlined setup card reads as an alarm; all three rings amber' (skeptic).
- 'Status: 160px of dead slate; the meter would be pinned at zero' (soul, system, usability).
- 'The ideas scope is chartjunk' (skeptic).
- 'Navy chat plates read as an editor's selection' (skeptic).

It keeps Sill's whole identity: the greeting standing on the Coming up rail, the tube's lit wire, the breathing NOW lamp and airglow, the station name in the rail, one-strip setup, the timetable To do whose stops are the ticks, Chat's single track with its lit ring, the dashed quiet weeks, and the Ideas line from home.

It gives up to make room:
- the tube's place at the top left of the board
- the hollow ring as the tick
- the long lit run (now NOW to stop one only)
- the third halo layer on the key word and a third of the board's outer halo
- Status's tall tally column
- the sideways starter row
- Lately added's right-aligned kind-word column
- the stacked header counts
- the green board edge and green plate edges
briefs.title: 'What needs a *plan*?', not yet tried. It keeps what the judges praised in this line's 'What needs planning?': the strongest invitation of its heat, one that 'cannot be answered no' and pulls in reminders, ideas and wishes as well as weekends (style, feedback). It fixes the one fault every lens named: the heavy 8-letter lit word. The lit word is now 'plan', the four-letter job word the panel prefers in 'What's our plan?', so the halo stays compact at display size and 'plan' sits right above the lit run of plans that answers it. It says FamilyDB's job: anything the family hands over that needs a plan, from a weekend to a reminder to a wish.
